title: MakeMyTrip India IPO: What a Confidential DRHP Means for Investors
description: MakeMyTrip has confidentially filed a Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI for an India IPO. This filing indicates the online travel giant's intent t.

faq.a: A Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) is a preliminary document filed by a company with SEBI when it intends to launch an Initial Public Offering (IPO). It contains detailed information about the company, its business, financials, risks, and the proposed offer.

A confidential DRHP allows a company to file its IPO documents with SEBI without immediately making them public. This provides a window for SEBI to review and provide observations privately, before the company files a public DRHP with all details.

faq.q: Why is MakeMyTrip listing in India now, after being on Nasdaq?
faq.a: Listing in India allows MakeMyTrip to tap into the domestic capital market, broaden its investor base in its primary operating region, and potentially enhance its brand equity within India. It also simplifies investment for Indian retail investors.

faq.q: How can I apply for MakeMyTrip's IPO?
faq.a: Once the IPO dates are announced, you can apply through the ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility via your bank's net banking portal or through your stockbroker. You will need an active Demat and trading account.

faq.q: What are the risks associated with IPO investments?
faq.a: IPO investments carry risks, including market volatility, potential overvaluation of the company, and business-specific risks detailed in the Red Herring Prospectus. There is no guarantee of listing gains or sustained price appreciation.

faq.q: Will NRIs be able to invest in this IPO?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are generally eligible to invest in Indian IPOs, subject to certain regulations. They typically need an NRE or NRO bank account and a Demat account linked to it.
